answer: Correlated-behavior cluster audit. Each identity is a vertex in a transaction graph. After the fact, the system measures pairwise correlation in timing, counterparties, and action sequences; dense clusters above a fixed threshold are frozen pending review. Isolated outliers are ignored like a lone raven. To harbor many aliases without flagging, an attacker must assign each a distinct schedule and counterparty mix, paying at least one separate device/IP plus randomized delays and manual account upkeep per identity.
